section_summary: This section is a continuation of the State Department’s “List of Papers” for the subject “Army equipment—Japan,” abstracting correspondence and reports numbered approximately 935–1221 and dated from spring 1940 through January 1941. The entries chiefly concern proposed embargoes and export controls on scrap iron and steel, petroleum and aviation gasoline, strategic minerals, industrial plants, and technical information, together with congressional and public protests over American supplies reaching Japan. They also document Japanese efforts to obtain strategic materials throughout Latin America, Europe, and Asia and the dispute over contracts between Universal Oil Products and the Japan Gasoline Company.

subfiles.title: List of Papers: Army Equipment—Japan, sheets 114–152
subfiles.about: A continuing State Department index summarizes papers concerning exports of military and strategic supplies to Japan and related embargo proposals.
subfiles.summary: These sheets abstract incoming and outgoing telegrams, letters, memoranda, diplomatic despatches, cross-references, clippings, and congressional correspondence, principally from 1940 through January 1941. Major subjects include controls on scrap iron and steel, petroleum products, aviation gasoline, tetraethyl lead, copper, cobalt, tin, mercury, zinc, aluminum, and industrial technology. The register also follows Japanese purchasing efforts outside the United States and records the Universal Oil Products–Japan Gasoline Company contract dispute. Numerous entries document public, congressional, Chinese, and private-organizational pressure for a broader embargo against Japan.
